samples.summary: The round store is keyed on the branch NAME alone, so two checkouts with the same branch name share one carry-forward store — the exact cross-context prompt-injection channel `branchKey` was written to close for detached HEAD
samples.evidence:
`reviewBase(branch)` (spec-to-pr.mjs:771-775) derives the base from the branch string only: `path.join(os.tmpdir(), "wafflebase-self-review", `${safe}-${hash}`)`, where `hash = sha1(branch)`. Nothing in the key identifies the repository, worktree, or remote — `cmdReview` calls it as `reviewBase(branch)` at line 902 with `branch = branchKey(git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD, …)`.

`branchKey`'s own docblock (lines 737-753) states the harm precisely for the detached-HEAD case: sharing a key means the checkouts "share a round counter … and, far worse, one carry-forward store — `priorFindingsFor` would read another change's verdicts and put their text into this round's verifier prompt." That harm is unaddressed for the much more common collision: two clones/worktrees on the same branch name.

Attack: a contributor controls both their branch NAME and its diff content. A maintainer who clones/worktrees the contributor's branch beside their own work — or simply has two checkouts on a common name such as `main`/`dev` — gets one shared base. `priorFindingsFor` (line 860-870) then reads `<base>/round-N/<lens>/verdict.json` written while reviewing the OTHER checkout and hands it to `prepareRoundInputs` → `panelArgs --prior-findings` (lines 1055-1062, 1086-1095), i.e. straight into the next round's verifier prompt. Lens verdict text is model output derived from the hostile diff, so a contributor who names their branch to collide can place chosen text in front of an agent session running in the maintainer's other checkout. The same collision also lets one checkout's rounds consume the other's three-round bound.

The per-user 0700 base limits this to a single user's checkouts, which is why this is `major` rather than `critical`. Fix: fold the repository identity (e.g. `git rev-parse --show-toplevel`, or the `origin` URL) into the hash alongside the branch.

samples.summary: `WAFFLEBASE_REVIEW_PANEL` turns an environment variable into an unrestricted arbitrary-script execution vector in a command agents are instructed to run automatically
samples.evidence:
`panelScript(env)` (spec-to-pr.mjs:793-796) returns `path.resolve(env.WAFFLEBASE_REVIEW_PANEL)` with no constraint on the path, and `cmdReview` spawns it as `execFileSync("node", panelArgs({ panel: panelScript(process.env), … }))` (lines 1084-1097). Any file on disk is executed as the invoking user, and the only thing that would tell the operator is that the panel behaved oddly — the resolved path is never printed.

The docblock argues "anyone who can set a variable in its environment can already run whatever they like". That holds for an interactive shell, but this command is now driven automatically by `.claude/commands/self-review.md` inside a repo checkout, and environment in that setting can come from tooling config a branch carries. It is also the one seam that would turn any future CI invocation of `spec-to-pr.mjs review` into remote code execution in a token-holding job (no workflow invokes it today — verified by grepping `.github/workflows` for `spec-to-pr`).

Hardening: constrain the override to a path under `HERE` (the sibling `scripts/agent` directory), or gate it on an explicit test marker (e.g. only honoured when `process.env.NODE_ENV === "test"`), and log the resolved panel path when it differs from the default.

samples.summary: `printable()` strips only C0/C1 controls, so model-authored findings can still reorder the terminal report with Unicode bidi/invisible controls
samples.evidence: `printable` (spec-to-pr.mjs:289-296) replaces `/[�--]/g` and nothing else, and its docblock claims model text is thereby made safe for the screen "a developer reads to decide whether the branch is clean". Unicode bidi overrides and isolates (U+202A-U+202E, U+2066-U+2069) and invisible/format characters (U+200B-U+200F, U+2060) survive and are honoured by every modern terminal, so a `summary` or `file` from a lens verdict can render in an order different from its bytes — the Trojan-Source display attack. Because `renderBlockingFindings` (lines 335-346) interpolates `f.file`, `f.line`, `f.summary` and the derived key into the report, a crafted finding can make a cited path or a blocking summary read as something else, which is the same outcome the CSI stripping exists to prevent. Add the bidi/format ranges to the replacement class.

samples.summary: `carryForwardFindings` says "PROJECT, never spread" but carries `mergedFrom` through wholesale, so unvalidated model-authored objects enter the next round's prior-findings file
samples.evidence:
The projection at prior-findings.mjs:166-179 rebuilds each finding from an explicit field list precisely so a lens cannot smuggle keys it chose to write (the docblock names `infra`). One level down that guarantee is dropped: `mergedFrom: Array.isArray(f.mergedFrom) ? f.mergedFrom : undefined` (line 174) passes the array's objects through unchanged, with every key and unbounded string length the model wrote.

The cloud copy this function mirrors does NOT do that — `.github/workflows/agent-review-panel.yml:1028` re-projects each entry: `mergedFrom: … .slice(0, 5).map((m) => ({ severity: norm(m.severity), summary: trim(m.summary, 500), adjudication: Number.isInteger(m.adjudication?.upheld) ? { upheld: m.adjudication.upheld } : undefined }))`. The local copy also skips the cloud's `norm(f.severity)` and `trim(f.summary, 2000)` / `trim(f.evidence, 2000)`.

Consumers do read these nested objects: `rebuttal.mjs:424` (`upheldCount`) reads `mergedFrom[].adjudication.upheld`, `severity.mjs:155` renders `m.severity`/`m.summary` into the human summary, and `fix-brief.mjs:179` renders `m.summary`. So a finding can carry arbitrary model-authored keys and unbounded prose into the file handed to the panel as `--prior-findings`, i.e. into the verifier prompt. Apply the same per-entry projection and caps the workflow applies.

samples.summary: The local `--rebuttals` path skips every validation and length cap the cloud rebuttal channel applies before author text reaches the adjudicator
samples.evidence:
`normalizeRebuttals` (spec-to-pr.mjs:632-636) only strips an `agent-review-` prefix and spreads the record; `readRebuttalRecords` (663-673) only checks the file parses to a non-empty array. The cloud path never hands the panel a record that has not been through `serializeRebuttal` (rebuttal.mjs:95-120: `trim(claim, 4000)`, `evidence.slice(0,10).map(e => trim(e,500))`, `neutral()` on every author field) and `parseRebuttalComment` (rebuttal.mjs:172-215: `v === REBUTTAL_VERSION`, non-empty `lens` and `file`, string coercion of evidence). `review-panel.mjs:2662-2667` accepts whatever the file holds (`raw.filter(r => r && typeof r === 'object')`) and `adjudicateRebuttals` (2309+) feeds it to `buildAdjudicatorPrompt`.

Prompt-fence escape is still covered — `buildAdjudicatorPrompt` applies `defence()` to `r.claim` and each evidence item at build time (rebuttal.mjs:492-495) — so this is hardening rather than an injection bypass. What is lost is the size bound and the shape/version validation: a hand-written (or agent-written, per `.claude/commands/self-review.md`) record can put an unbounded `claim` and an unbounded `evidence` array in front of the one component permitted to remove a finding from the gate. Route the local file through the same caps (reuse `serializeRebuttal`/`parseRebuttalComment`, or apply `trim`/`neutral` in `normalizeRebuttals`).
searchedFor: grep rebuttals in review-panel.mjs (arg parsing at 2661-2667, adjudicateRebuttals at 2309)

samples.summary: `blockingFindingsIn` uses an id read back from `panel.json` as a path segment with no validation
samples.evidence: `blockingFindingsIn(outDir, lensIds)` does `readFileSync(path.join(outDir, lens, "verdict.json"))` (spec-to-pr.mjs:877) where `lens` comes from `panel.filter(...).map((p) => p.id)` (line 1112) — parsed from `panel.json` on disk (line 1104) with no shape check. An id such as `../../..//etc/…` would read outside the round directory and print the result through `renderBlockingFindings`. Today `panel.json` is written by `review-panel.mjs` from the trusted lens manifest and the base directory is enforced 0700/owned-by-us, so this is not currently reachable; it is defence in depth on a predictable path whose guard has already been reworked four times (see docs/tasks/active/20260917-self-review-loop-todo.md). Validate the id against `/^[a-z0-9-]+$/`, or restrict it to the directory entries actually present in `outDir`. Note `roundDirsToClear` (line 732) already gets this right by regenerating `round-${n}` from a parsed integer rather than trusting the dirent name.

samples.summary: The new contributor-facing text states the panel's admission rule and the `@claude loop` privilege more permissively than the workflows actually enforce
samples.evidence:
CONTRIBUTING.md:201-205 says the panel "admits a PR only when its branch starts with `agent/` or it carries the `agent:managed` label" and tells the reader to "Comment … `@claude loop` to opt into the panel plus its auto-fix rounds." Two authorization conditions are omitted, both in the permissive direction, and CONTRIBUTING's audience is mostly fork-based contributors:

1. `.github/workflows/agent-review-panel.yml:167` additionally requires `github.event.workflow_run.head_repository.full_name == github.repository`, and `agent-iterate-ci.yml:56` the same — a fork PR is never admitted, label or not. (docs/design/agentic-dev-loop.md in this same change does say "same-repo only" for `@claude loop`, so the two docs disagree.)
2. `.github/workflows/agent-loop.yml:66-77` fails the run unless the commenter's collaborator permission is `admin`/`maintain`/`write` — `@claude loop` is maintainer-only, not something a contributor can invoke on their own PR.

A contributor following this text will believe they opted a fork PR into automated review and auto-fix when nothing ran. State the same-repo requirement and mark `@claude loop` as maintainer-only.

verdict.reason: Verified in-repo and the finding is accurate. `reviewBase` (spec-to-pr.mjs:771-775) derives the round-store path purely from the branch string — `safe` (sanitized name) plus `sha1(branch).slice(0,8)` under `os.tmpdir()/wafflebase-self-review/` — with no repository, worktree, or remote component; I grepped scripts/agent for `show-toplevel`/repo-identity inputs and found none feeding this path. `cmdReview` uses it as the default base at :902 with `branch = branchKey(...)` from :896. The carry-forward chain is exactly as described: `priorFindingsFor` reads `<base>/round-N/<lens>/verdict.json` (:860-870) and the result flows through `prepareRoundInputs` (:1055-1058) into `panelArgs`'s `priorFile` on the spawned panel (:1084-1097), plus the dry-run read at :1023. So any two checkouts sharing a branch name share one base, one round counter, and one carry-forward store, and lens verdict text (model output derived from a hostile diff) from one checkout is fed into the verifier prompt of a session running in the other. The file's own `branchKey` docblock (:736-753) names this exact harm — "one carry-forward store — `priorFindingsFor` would read another change's verdicts and put their text into this round's verifier prompt" — but only closes it for detached HEAD. No guard makes it unreachable: `unsafeBaseReason` (:500-571, checks at :522-570) enforces leaf 0700/ownership and no foreign-writable ancestor, which defends only against *other* users; two checkouts by the same user pass every check and still collide. In lane as a cross-context prompt-injection / sensitive-data-exposure channel into an agent session holding developer credentials — the same threat the file itself documents at :508-512 — and blocking at major severity under this rubric.
